title: Going Where, by Whom, and at What Time: Next Location Prediction Considering User Preference and Temporal Regularity

problem.claim: Next location prediction is a human mobility modeling task supporting downstream applications such as location-based recommendation and transportation planning.

gap.claim: Prior studies underrepresent explicit user preference information and underuse the next location's arrival time as a determinant of prediction.

contributions.claim: MCLP explicitly models user preference and next arrival time as contextual information for next location prediction.
The model extracts location-type preferences with a topic model and constructs an arrival-time embedding with a multi-head-attention estimator.
MCLP uses a Transformer to mine sequential patterns and integrate multiple contextual signals for next location prediction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two real-world mobility datasets reportedly show that MCLP outperforms baseline methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Next location prediction is important for human mobility modeling and downstream applications.
Existing research insufficiently represents user preference and next-location arrival time.
MCLP addresses the gap by modeling user preference and next arrival time as context.
The method combines topic-based preference extraction, attention-based arrival-time estimation, and Transformer-based sequence modeling.
The authors report improved performance over baselines on two real-world mobility datasets.

source_observation.claim: The model integrates user preference and temporal context into next location prediction.

interpretation.claim: Prediction may improve when behaviorally meaningful context is modeled alongside sequential patterns.

application.claim: For mobility prediction tasks, consider combining individual preference signals with time-related context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination generalizes beyond the two reported mobility datasets.
